content.text: Quick comparison of element geometry between baseline and current.

I fixed the layout bug. The remaining diffs look like font-rendering differences between machines, so I haven't approved the baselines.

**The bug:** in `site/css/styles.css`, the `.card` rule had `position: absolute` instead of `position: relative`. That took every card out of normal flow. The call-to-action banner was hidden behind the cards, the three cards overlapped and stretched to the page height, and the footer was pushed out of place. I changed it back to `relative` (around line 4169).

**After the fix:** I re-ran the visual tests. Every element on the desktop page now has the same position and size as the baseline. The only differences are text widths a few pixels off, for example the navbar brand at 145 px against 142 px and "Services" at 80 px against 82 px. That shifts text by a pixel or two, which is why desktop still shows 3.2% of pixels as different and phone 5.4%. I found no CSS rule that explains it. The baselines were captured on a different OS build (kernel `6.18.44-fc-v653`, now `v819`), so this is most likely font rendering. I haven't confirmed that.

**Baselines:** both snapshots still show as "changed", and approving them is your decision. Before you do, I'd check the phone diff yourself. I haven't looked at it, since the large page-height change was on desktop. If the remaining diffs look right to you, run `npx testivai approve --all`, or tell me and I'll approve them.

STATUS: DONE
